title: Intermittent tenant elevation from legacy API key mapping during cluster cutover
creator: Ishani Patel
description: Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported rare cases where requests authenticated with older (pre-rollout) API keys briefly appeared to have broader org-scoped access during a rolling cluster cutover. This manifested as cross-tenant reads (metadata only) in audit logs for up to 30s during specific node handoffs. The behavior is intermittent and correlated with key-format migration and our fastpath cache invalidation window used during cutover.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have a Dedicated cluster at v2.4 with legacy api-key mappings in the keyring and fastpath cache enabled.
2) Start a rolling cutover that replaces per-node key mapping service with the new central mapper.
3) Issue concurrent requests using a legacy key bound to tenant A while rapid refresh traffic rebinds tenant mappings.
4) Observe audit/log entries showing the request accepted for tenant B for a small subset of control-plane validated endpoints (metadata endpoints).
root_cause: A race between on-node fastpath cache eviction and the central mapping upgrade. During the cutover we briefly accepted requests using an older key-to-namespace table before the new central mapper fully populated the node-local resolver. A fallback path mistakenly consulted a permissive legacy binder that only validated key signatures and returned a broader default namespace object for backward compatibility. Combined with small clock skew and a 20–40s grace window for rotated keys, this allowed a handful of requests to be authorized against the wrong tenant's metadata endpoints.
mitigation_and_patch:
Short-term mitigation: 1) Disable the permissive legacy binder during cutovers (feature-flagged) and force strict verification against the central mapper. 2) Reduce the grace window for rotated keys from 40s to 5s for Dedicated/Private clusters during rolling upgrades.
Permanent patch: 1) Change resolver logic so on node-local misses we fail closed instead of consulting legacy binder. 2) Add an opportunistic pre-warm handshake during cutover to populate node caches before traffic is cut over. PR: GH-rlwd/infra#5987
rollout_plan:
1) Merge hotfix branch to release-2.4.1 and run smoke tests in staging dedicated cluster (canary tenant).
2) Coordinate with site reliability to schedule low-traffic window for rolling release.
3) Use feature flag to disable legacy binder on a single zone, monitor for false-positives, then progressively enable cluster-wide.
4) Post-deploy increase audit sampling and run scripted request patterns to validate no cross-tenant metadata reads are observed.
tests: Unit: add tests for resolver fallback paths to assert fail-closed behavior. Integration: simulate cutover with concurrent requests and verify no tenant leakage. E2E: gated runbook that executes on staging dedicated cluster with increased audit sampling. Test artifacts: confluence doc and test harness repo runbook referenced below.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create a temporary alert 'auth.unexpected.cross_tenant_reads' if audit sampling shows >0 cross-tenant metadata reads for 1m. Dashboard: auth/resolver/fastpath-miss-rate and audit/cross-tenant-sampling. Keep 7d retention for increased sampling period. On alert page runbook points to ENG-143210.
customer_communications: Notify impacted customers who filed escalations with an interim mitigation summary and ETA for patch (targeted rolling release within 72h). Provide post-mortem with root cause and verification steps. Draft message in support tracker: SUP-7863. Escalation owners: Samir Chen (support) and Priya Rao (eng-relations).
